To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the orf virus reinfects sheep and causes a local skin lesion that is characterized by limited virus replication and an activated CD8+ cytotoxic T cell response.

orf virus infection of the skin is associated with a cytolytic T cell response that is characterized by a high proportion of activated CD8+ cytolytic T cells expressing a cell-associated serine esterase (BLT-esterase) in the skin and afferents lymph.

orf virus infection in sheep is associated with the recruitment and activation of CTLs to the site of infection and that the activated CTLs express BLT-esterases and mediate cytolysis of autologously infected cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the skin and its lymphatics in the immune response to infection.
understanding the role of T cell-mediated immunity in the pathogenesis and resolution of orf virus infection.
the role of CD8+ T lymphocyte in viral infection and the mechanisms involved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the orf virus reinfects the skin, and that this reinfection stimulates the recruitment of cytolytic CD8+ T lymphocytes to the site of reinfection, which then express the cytolytic associated serine proteases, BLT-estrase and cathepsin G.
CD8+ T lymphocytes are involved in the control of the orf virus infection in sheep.
the CTL response is a major effector mechanism of orf virus immunity and that BLT-esterse is a useful marker for CTL activation in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
orf virus infection of sheep is characterized by a rapid and efficient CTL response that limits virus replication and prevents systemic spread.
the orf virus is a model for the study of the immune response in the skin, and in particular for the role of CD8+ T lymphocytes in the control of viral infection in this tissue.
orf virus infection of sheep is characterized by a rapid and limited viral replication, which induces an activated cytolytic cell response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the skin is an important site for the development and maintenance of the immune response to orf virus reinfections.
the CTL response in the sheep skin is not as vigorous as that seen in the skin of other species such as the mouse and the pig.
BLT-esterases are useful markers for activated cytolytically active T cells and may be used to study the role of these cells in vivo.
